**Finding: MINCOMMIT — compliant (no redline proposed).**

We reviewed every candidate location (Product Forecast §11.0–11.3, Purchase of Products §6.0, PO Cancellation §6.1, Inventory §13.0–13.4, Supply Flexibility §13.2/Appendix 4, Requirements Accuracy Appendix 2, Premium Cost §9.0, and Rights/Prices Upon Termination §5.2–5.3).

- **No minimum purchase or volume commitment:** forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product" (p0882); production follows "actual intake of IBM Customer Orders" (p0870).
- **Exit retained:** we may cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time (p0722); no liability for unused supply flexibility (p0927).
- **Only volume-linked exposure** is the Requirements Accuracy mechanic (p0903 / Appendix 2), which is a percentage-of-material-cost true-up for Parts MSL actually bought on our forecast — a true-up, not a shortfall penalty, and not term-length take-or-pay.
- Termination inventory buy-backs (§5.2) are bounded by Supply Flexibility and exclude cancellable Parts, so they are wind-down cost recovery rather than a purchase commitment.

The bargain therefore meets the fallback (and substantially the preferred) position, so no redline. Business-side check only: the Appendix 2 percentages/thresholds are redacted — confirm they are cost-recovery rather than punitive.
